chapter: Fellow musicians: Kirk, Bunk, Parker, McShann
title: Emil Williams sent for Lovett to come to Kansas City
summary: Lovett says he came alone because pianist Emil Williams, whom he had played with eight years in Shreveport, sent for him.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, who brought up -- you up here, Baby?
Well, Emil Williams, the piano player, wonderful, marvelous, he's a marvelous piano player, and he sent for me to come here.
No, right next to the local there. What was the name of that place next to the local, that big
hall right next to the local -- oh anyway I can't think of it. All right.

Well anyway, he sent for me to play in there. He was playing there, you see; yeah, Emil played there and that's when I came here, Emil sent for me. Well, I'll tell you, Roland Bruce told him about me, you understand, which I knew Emil before he came here. See I played with him in Shreveport for eight years.
He came and then he sent for me to come to Kansas City.
